correctness.rationale: For a graph isomorphic to K_{2n-2,2,...,2}, a small-part vertex has cyclicizer size c+2, so the foundational divisibility lemma gives c|2. If c=1, the large part plus the cyclicizer is a finite locally cyclic subgroup of order 2n-1 inside a group of order 4n-1, contradicting Lagrange. Thus c=2. The large cyclicizer is a cyclic normal subgroup K of order 2n; every outside vertex lies in a cyclic order-four small cyclicizer and squares to the same involution z. For x outside K, (xk)^2=z for every k in K implies xkx^{-1}=k^{-1}. Hence H has the dicyclic presentation and order 4n.

value.rationale: The theorem extends a foundational uniqueness phenomenon from generalized quaternion 2-groups to the complementary dicyclic family and does so by reconstructing group structure, not by computing a routine graph invariant. The noncyclic graph forces both the cyclic index-two subgroup and the inversion action, so the result is a natural group-recognition statement.
